desc: Learning experience platform letting employees track learning from many sources, with skills and career development tools for enterprises.
markets: Enterprise customers, mainly in the US; international customers not confirmed.
rationale: Corporate learning software; F1 hospitality could support enterprise sales, but marketing scale is modest.

name: Edgio
desc: Content delivery and edge cloud company formed in 2022 when Limelight Networks acquired Edgecast, serving video streaming and enterprises.
markets: Served streaming and enterprise customers across North America, Europe and Asia; the business has been broken up.
rationale: Bankrupt company whose assets were sold off and whose brand no longer operates; no F1 sponsorship case.
changed: Filed for bankruptcy in 2024; assets sold, including to Akamai

name: Metagenomi
desc: Biotechnology company developing gene editing therapies using novel CRISPR systems discovered from metagenomic sequencing.
markets: Pre-revenue, US-based research with industry collaborations; no consumer markets or verified international operations.
rationale: Pre-revenue therapeutics developer with no consumer brand and no commercial products; weak F1 fit overall.

name: NEAR
desc: Blockchain protocol and platform for scalable decentralised applications and AI agents, developed by the NEAR Foundation and Near Inc.
markets: Developer and user community worldwide around the NEAR network; ecosystem partners in several regions.
rationale: Blockchain brand with global community; crypto firms are frequent F1 sponsors, so visibility and partnership fit are plausible.

name: o9 Solutions
desc: Cloud planning software, the o9 Digital Brain platform, for demand planning, supply chain, revenue management and integrated business planning.
markets: Large enterprise customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, with offices on several continents.
rationale: Enterprise planning software with global clients; F1 logistics and data themes plus client hospitality make it plausible.

name: PagerDuty
desc: Digital operations platform that alerts engineering teams to incidents, coordinates response and automates workflows, with AI features.
markets: Engineering teams in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, mostly US customers.
rationale: Developer operations vendor; F1 technology and hospitality fit, as Dynatrace and Splunk already sponsor.

name: Builder.ai
desc: No-code, AI-assisted software development company founded in 2016 as Engineer.ai that assembled custom apps from reusable templates.
markets: Customers in the UK, US, Middle East and other regions before the company collapsed.
rationale: Insolvent company that has collapsed and ceased trading, so there is no F1 case.

name: Dragos
desc: Industrial cybersecurity company protecting operational technology networks in power plants, utilities, manufacturing and oil and gas.
markets: Industrial customers in North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Industrial cyber vendor selling to energy and manufacturing; F1 hospitality and technology exposure fit, with cyber peers already sponsoring.

name: IronNet Cybersecurity
desc: Network detection and response company founded in 2014 by former NSA director Keith Alexander, offering collective defence cyber services.
markets: US government and enterprise customers; the business went through bankruptcy and no longer operates.
rationale: Bankrupt cyber vendor that no longer operates, so there is no F1 sponsorship case.

name: Polygon
desc: Blockchain network and ecosystem for scaling Ethereum, launched in 2017 as Matic Network and used by apps such as Aave.
markets: Developers and users worldwide, with large ecosystem activity in Asia, Europe and the US.
rationale: Crypto brand seeking global user growth; crypto firms already sponsor F1, giving visibility and partnership precedent.

name: SellersFi
desc: Fintech providing financing to e-commerce sellers, using AI credit scoring and marketplace integrations such as Amazon.
markets: E-commerce sellers on online marketplaces, mainly in the US; international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Niche lender to online sellers with a small brand and US focus; F1 fit is weak.

name: SoundHound
desc: Voice AI company, founded in 2005 as a music recognition app, selling voice assistants and conversational AI to automakers.
markets: Customers in automotive, restaurants and devices across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Voice AI brand with automotive customers; F1 suits technology showcase and B2B hospitality, with AI partners already present.

name: YouGov
desc: Market research and data analytics company, founded in 2000, running online panels and syndicated research for brands, media and sports.
markets: Offices and panels across the UK, US, Europe, Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Sponsorship research is a core product, so F1 offers client hospitality and fan data credibility across international markets.

name: AEye
desc: Develops adaptive, high-performance lidar systems for automotive, trucking and industrial applications.
markets: Automotive and industrial customers and partners; international sales not confirmed.
rationale: Lidar supplier with limited brand marketing; F1 technology showcase possible, but fit is modest.

name: Chronosphere
desc: Cloud-native observability platform helping engineering teams monitor and control metrics, traces, logs and the cost of data.
markets: Engineering teams at large technology companies, mainly in the US; other regions not confirmed.
rationale: Observability vendor; F1 technology showcase fits, though Dynatrace and Splunk already occupy the category.

name: Cloud.ru
desc: Russian cloud services and AI provider, formerly the cloud arm of Sberbank, offering cloud infrastructure, platform and AI services.
markets: Russian business and public sector customers; sanctions limit international activity.
rationale: Sanctioned bank-owned Russian cloud provider with a domestic focus; F1 sponsorship is practically impossible.

name: CloudPay
desc: Global payroll services and software provider managing payroll for multinational companies across around 130 countries.
markets: Multinational clients with payroll across about 130 countries in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Payroll provider for multinationals; F1 hospitality suits large enterprise clients, and HR vendors such as Workday already sponsor.

name: CoachHub
desc: Digital coaching platform, founded in 2018, giving corporate employees access to certified coaches worldwide.
markets: Corporate clients in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific, with coaches in many countries.
rationale: Corporate coaching brand with international growth; F1 hospitality and performance themes fit, and BetterUp already partners with F1.
